title: 2939. Maximum Xor Product

examples.explanation: For x = 2, (a XOR x) = 14 and (b XOR x) = 7. Hence, (a XOR x) * (b XOR x) = 98. It can be shown that 98 is the maximum value of (a XOR x) * (b XOR x) for all 0 <= x < 2n.
For x = 25, (a XOR x) = 31 and (b XOR x) = 30. Hence, (a XOR x) * (b XOR x) = 930. It can be shown that 930 is the maximum value of (a XOR x) * (b XOR x) for all 0 <= x < 2n.
For x = 5, (a XOR x) = 4 and (b XOR x) = 3. Hence, (a XOR x) * (b XOR x) = 12. It can be shown that 12 is the maximum value of (a XOR x) * (b XOR x) for all 0 <= x < 2n.

hints: Iterate over bits from most significant to least significant.
For the ith bit, if both a and b have the same value, we can always make x’s ith bit different from a and b, so a ^ x and b ^ x both have the ith bit set.
Otherwise, we can only set the ith bit of one of a ^ x or b ^ x. Depending on the previous bits of a ^ x or b ^ x, we should set the smaller value’s ith bit.
